name: Porto Cristo – Bayo's landing on Mallorca
story: Mallorca sided with the coup in July 1936. On 16 August Captain Alberto Bayo, with Catalan and Valencian militia and naval support, landed on the east coast at Porto Cristo and Punta Amer (Sa Coma), renaming the port 'Porto Rojo'. The attackers were poorly coordinated, and the defenders were reinforced by Italian aircraft and the Fascist Arconovaldo Bonaccorsi ('Conde Rossi'). The counter-attack from 27 August drove the Republicans back, and they re-embarked by 4 September, leaving equipment behind. Captured militiamen and local leftists were executed; in 2020 excavations at Son Coletes cemetery in Manacor found remains of milicianos and two nurses.
see: The harbour and beaches of Porto Cristo and Sa Coma, where the landing and fighting took place. There is no major monument on the shore; Son Coletes cemetery in Manacor has the excavated grave site.
plan: Walk the harbour and the Passeig de la Sirena, then drive 12 km to Manacor for Son Coletes cemetery. Pairs with a visit to the Drach caves.
